title: Targeting the HIF-1alpha/IL-1beta Axis in Macrophages With the Novel Inhibitor LJ-6 Mitigates Adipose Tissue Inflammation in Cellular and Ex Vivo Models.
authors: Gao, Min; Liu, Mengyuan; Chu, Anran; Deng, Sisi; Gao, Jingsong; Li, Shasha; Jiang, Dongsheng; Shen, Yuqing; Wang, Xinyue; Lei, Saifei; Wu, Rui; Jiang, Haowen; Li, Jia; Li, Jinlong; Wang, Xinyi; Peng, Chang
one_liner_zh: 该文研究小分子抑制剂LJ-6靶向HIF-1alpha/IL-1beta轴缓解脂肪组织炎症，虽涉及分子对接与动力学模拟，但核心是药物-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，仅HRE报告基因间接涉及转录调控，与本课题TF-DNA结合机制关联较弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sustained activation of adipose tissue macrophages (ATMs) drives metabolic dysfunction in obesity, with the hypoxia-inducible factor-1alpha (HIF-1alpha)/interleukin-1beta (IL-1beta) axis being a core signaling pathway. However, specific strategies targeting this axis are still lacking. Here, we aimed to identify novel compounds capable of disrupting this pathway. METHODS: We screened a natural product library for inhibitors of IL-1beta expression in macrophages. The hit compound LJ-6 was then evaluated in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs) and in a physiologically relevant model using conditioned medium from obese adipose tissue. Mechanism of action was investigated via Western blotting, molecular docking, dynamics simulations, and hypoxia-response element (HRE)-luciferase reporter assays with site-directed mutagenesis. RESULTS: LJ-6 was identified as a potent inhibitor of IL-1beta. It dose-dependently suppressed IL-1beta in both LPS-induced and obese adipose tissue-conditioned medium-induced macrophage inflammation. Mechanistically, LJ-6 reduced HIF-1alpha protein stability. Molecular docking and mutagenesis studies supported an interaction involving the Tyr92 and His197 residues of HIF-1alpha, and suggested that this interaction is critical for its inhibitory function on the HIF-1alpha/IL-1beta axis. CONCLUSIONS: This study identifies the natural compound LJ-6 as a novel direct inhibitor of HIF-1alpha. By binding to HIF-1alpha, LJ-6 effectively suppresses the HIF-1alpha/IL-1beta axis in macrophages, thereby reducing IL-1beta-driven inflammatory responses in cellular and ex vivo models of obesity-associated adipose tissue inflammation, and thus represents a promising lead compound for therapeutic development.
abstract_zh: 背景：脂肪组织巨噬细胞（ATMs）的持续激活驱动肥胖中的代谢功能障碍，其中缺氧诱导因子-1α（HIF-1α）/白细胞介素-1β（IL-1β）轴是核心信号通路。然而，针对该轴的特异性策略仍缺乏。本研究旨在识别能够破坏该通路的新型化合物。方法：我们筛选了一个天然产物库，以寻找巨噬细胞中IL-1β表达的抑制剂。随后，在脂多糖（LPS）刺激的骨髓来源巨噬细胞（BMDMs）以及使用肥胖脂肪组织条件培养基的生理相关模型中，评估了命中化合物LJ-6。通过Western blotting、分子对接、动力学模拟以及缺氧反应元件（HRE）-荧光素酶报告基因实验结合定点突变，研究了其作用机制。结果：LJ-6被鉴定为IL-1β的有效抑制剂。在LPS诱导和肥胖脂肪组织条件培养基诱导的巨噬细胞炎症中，LJ-6均剂量依赖性地抑制IL-1β。机制上，LJ-6降低了HIF-1α蛋白稳定性。分子对接和突变研究支持涉及HIF-1α的Tyr92和His197残基的相互作用，并提示该相互作用对其抑制HIF-1α/IL-1β轴的功能至关重要。结论：本研究将天然化合物LJ-6鉴定为HIF-1α的新型直接抑制剂。通过结合HIF-1α，LJ-6有效抑制巨噬细胞中的HIF-1α/IL-1β轴，从而在肥胖相关脂肪组织炎症的细胞和离体模型中减少IL-1β驱动的炎症反应，因此代表了治疗开发的有前景的先导化合物。
